The cost is an offline calibration and search pipeline: model-specific power-transform fitting, per-expert error estimation across three configurations, combination with spectra/variance/precision-decay priors, and added deployment metadata rather than a simple uniform quantizer. It can fail if the contrast target misweights experts for a specific workload, if the joint gate/up/down error estimate does not transfer to production data, or in the minority of settings where perplexity does not improve despite better KL and token agreement. 0 independent implementations, 81 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RoLaQ: Joint Rotation and Range Calibration for 2-Bit KV Caches in Multi-Head Latent Attention
item.description: RoLaQ replaces BF16 or coarser 2-bit KV cache storage in multi-head latent attention with an offline joint rotation and quantization-range calibration, keeping model weights frozen. The cost is a one-time calibration procedure with prediction-matching and attention-output supervision, plus reliance on a custom SGLang implementation; runtime cost is a rotation applied to the latent cache. It can fail on models without MLA architecture, when the calibration data does not match the deployment distribution, or if the SGLang kernels are unavailable for the reader's serving stack. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
item.description: ORL replaces standard multi-step DLM denoising (and, in single-request serving, autoregressive decoding with speculative decoding such as EAGLE3/DFlash) by carrying residual predictive distributions across denoising steps and training on-policy with an entropy-contraction objective, served via the dlmrt engine. It costs a residual-learning fine-tuning run (36 H100-hours and 4.2M self-generated tokens on LLaDA-2.1-mini, feasible on a modest budget), dependence on a custom engine, and added system complexity in residual capture, block-diffusion attention, and packed training. It can fail because results are demonstrated on a small set of converted or existing DLMs, the Pareto gains are shown mainly for single-request serving rather than batched production traffic, and quality parity may not hold on task distributions outside the reported benchmarks. 3 independent implementations, 35 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sliced Wasserstein Sketches with Error Certificates
item.description: The method replaces storing and comparing full empirical distributions (or large equal-mass quantizations) in sliced Wasserstein pipelines with optimal free-weight M-atom quantizations per projection, costing O(LM) comparison time and the implementation complexity of the quantization plus residual-energy bookkeeping. It adds certified error bounds and covariance recovery from residual energies, but equal-mass sketches can converge more slowly than the O(M^{-1}) rate for optimal sketches. It can fail when the finite (2+delta) moment assumption does not hold, when too few projections are used for covariance recovery, or when the workload does not actually compare probability distributions, making the machinery irrelevant. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PRISM: Transfer and Limits of Activation Interventions in Tool-Calling Language Models
item.description: Replaces prompt-level guardrails or safety fine-tuning with inference-time activation interventions whose steering directions are estimated from a quantized NF4 copy and transferred across languages and model scales. Costs are activation-access instrumentation, per-direction estimation experiments, and a residual inference overhead, all feasible on a single 24 GB GPU for 8B-class open models but requiring weight access that third-party APIs do not provide. Can fail when directions estimated on few scenarios do not generalize to unseen tools or domains, when interventions degrade benign tool-calling behavior, or when transfer to larger models (up to 70B) exceeds the available memory budget. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Task-Phase-Conditioned Expert Routing Is Not a Reliable Proxy for Quantization Sensitivity in MoE FFN Tensors
item.description: The method replaces uniform (flat) bit-width allocation for MoE expert FFN tensors with layer-wise allocation derived from routing statistics (entropy, CV, Jaccard phase-fragility, top-1 strength), tuned by coordinate descent under a fixed average bpw budget. It costs a custom routing-capture and profiling pipeline in a modified inference runtime plus tuning compute, with no measured quality benefit over uniform quantization. What fails is the core premise: routing behavior is an unvalidated proxy for per-layer quantization cost, so guided allocation performs no better than random reallocation, and aggressive budgets lose quality regardless of allocation strategy. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Long-Context Drafting Does Not Require Long-Context Drafters
item.description: Replaces training or fine-tuning a long-context drafter (or shipping a multi-token head) by reusing released short-context drafters with two inference-time mechanisms: bounding the drafter's attention cache and re-basing rotary indices into the trained range, implemented as one vLLM-side configuration. No weights are modified, the single tunable saturates early, and drafter compute cost becomes constant rather than growing with context. Adoption fails if the speculative cost per emitted token exceeds matched target-only cost, if either mechanism is removed, or when no compatible released drafter exists for the target model. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Flexible Doubly Robust Proximal Causal Inference for Censored Outcomes
item.description: PSB replaces parametric bridge models in proximal causal inference for right-censored time-to-event outcomes with flexible kernel (PSB-K) and neural (PSB-N) bridge learners offering doubly robust estimation of survival curves. The cost is substantial statistical engineering: it requires valid proxy variables for unmeasured confounding, careful bridge-function estimation, and specialized survival-analysis expertise rather than any GPU or serving infrastructure. It can fail when proxies are weakened or invalid, under heavy censoring, and its benchmark advantages are dataset-dependent (PSB-K wins on SEM/ACTG, PSB-N on Framingham), so no estimator is uniformly reliable. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
item.description: SALTO replaces repeated forward/adjoint solves through a numerical PDE simulator for finite-amplitude source inversion with a single trained Koopman model whose lifted transpose propagates sensors backward in one solve and answers candidate events with an encoder pass and an inner product. The cost is an offline training stage plus three structural constraints (anchoring to the simulator's linearized propagator, centered observables, block-triangular propagator), which require access to the simulator's tangent linearization and observable training data. It can fail when events are far outside the training amplitude or location distribution, when no differentiable simulator or its linearization is available, and its accuracy guarantees hold only in the vanishing-amplitude limit rather than for arbitrary perturbations. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Probabilistic Optical-Layer Surrogate for Risk-Aware Control-Plane Decision Making
item.description: The method replaces analytical impairment models, deterministic learned predictors, and quantile-regression estimates in optical transport control planes with a conditional generative model that outputs full distributions over OSNR, Q-margin, and feasibility, enabling runtime tail-risk queries without per-decision retraining. The cost is training on validated optical simulator traces plus integration into a network controller, with inference latency claimed as low enough for live decision making but not quantified in the abstract. It can fail through distribution shift between simulator training traces and real hardware behavior, despite the paper's cross-emulator and GNPy validation studies. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Helix: A Unified Programmable Accelerator for Diverse Krylov Subspace Solvers
item.description: Helix replaces single-solver or reconfiguration-per-solver FPGA designs for Krylov subspace methods with a unified programmable architecture built on shared computational primitives, a DSL compiler, and programmable datapaths. It costs an FPGA prototyping flow (Xilinx Alveo U55C class hardware with HBM), a custom DSL toolchain, and 4.7% LUT / 4.0% FF plus 0.25%-0.57% execution-time overhead for programmability. It can fail for the reader because it addresses sparse linear system solving in scientific computing, not LLM inference or training, and requires FPGA hardware and HLS expertise that a GPU-and-API-constrained ML team does not possess. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches
item.description: RoPERelay replaces the default practice of retaining original full-history RoPE coordinates in a sparse KV cache; after selection, it compacts coordinates in an order-preserving way by inverse-rotating and re-rotating cached key phases and synchronizing the current query, without renewed selection, re-prefill, or extra cache budget. It costs roughly 1%-3% additional request latency in the evaluated configurations plus implementation complexity in the inference path, with no extra memory or cache footprint. It can fail if the serving stack does not expose per-key positional manipulation, if the model uses non-RoPE positional schemes, or if gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated long-term memory tasks and selectors to the reader's workloads. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Long Context to Selective Memory:A Survey of Memory-Centric Compression for Large Language Models
item.description: This survey reframes the isolated practices of prompt compression, KV-cache management, and retrieval augmentation as a unified memory-management problem, distinguishing compute-active from compute-inactive memory and modeling operations (offloading, recall, materialization, eviction, forgetting) as budgeted state transitions rather than proposing a deployable method. It imposes no runtime cost itself, but adopting its lifecycle-aware design perspective adds architectural complexity to systems that must decide which information enters costly inference, when, and in what form. Because it is a taxonomy and cost model without validated implementations, applying its framework prematurely could yield over-engineered memory hierarchies whose eviction and forgetting policies silently discard information needed for task correctness. 2 independent implementations, 128 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair
item.description: MemScope replaces coarse feedback-driven (score- or summary-based) self-evolution of memory architectures with a Patch Agent that inspects raw execution traces, runtime memory state, and architecture code to apply bounded, in-place edits. It costs an additional tool-using agent loop over traces and code during the offline evolution phase, plus trace/memory-state logging infrastructure, rather than inference-time overhead. It can fail when failure localization from traces is incorrect, when bounded edits overfit the evaluation tasks (gains on ALFWorld are larger than on xBench), or when provider-identity and memory-compatibility constraints block needed changes, and results are reported on specific benchmarks that may not transfer to the reader's workload. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentEval: Evidence-Bounded Assessment of Stateful Agents
item.description: Replaces task-completion-only or hash-only evaluation of stateful agents with a contract-bound executable assessment record that separates agent actions, evidential support, and conclusion validity. Costs implementation and maintenance of state/event capture, report qualification, and case-maintenance infrastructure, adding engineering complexity rather than model latency or GPU memory. Can fail through incomplete or misconfigured evidence capture, contract definitions that do not match real obligations, and per-case review overhead that does not scale to high-volume production traffic. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.
